1) the use of pedicle screw instrumentation in conjunction with interbody fusion provides the most reliable means of achieving fusion and 2) the most important determinant in predicting a good outcome is the patient's preoperative clinical status.

the incidence of adjacent segment degeneration is not significantly different between patients treated with fusion and those treated with decompression alone, that the incidence of pseudarthrosis in patients treated with fusion is approximately 20%, and that the incidence of complications in patients treated with interbody fusion is approximately 10% to 20%.

1) fusion is a safe procedure that can be performed in most patients; 2) fusion is a procedure that is not indicated for all patients; 3) fusion should be considered for patients with persistent symptoms after decompression; and 4) fusion should be performed with the goal of achieving fusion and not merely instrumentation.
